findings.issue: Source: 'this rich and goodly armour, which no man has ever yet borne upon his shoulders'. Candidate: 'No man has ever carried anything like it on his shoulders' adds a comparison ('anything like it') the source does not state.
findings.fix: Saffron-robed Dawn was rising from the streams of Oceanus to bring light to mortals and immortals when Thetis reached the ships, carrying the armor the god had given her. She found her son lying across the body of Patroclus, weeping bitterly. Many of his followers were weeping around him too. The goddess walked in among them and took his hand in hers. “My son,” she said, “however much we grieve, we must let this man lie. It was heaven’s will that he fell. Now take this rich and beautiful armor from Hephaestus. No man has ever yet carried it on his shoulders.”

findings.issue: Source 'I am in great heaviness'; candidate 'I am in deep heaviness' keeps an archaic, unidiomatic phrase a general reader may trip on.
findings.fix: She wept as she spoke, and the women joined in her lament. They seemed to cry for Patroclus, but in truth each was weeping for her own sorrows. The elders of the Achaeans gathered around Achilles and begged him to eat. He groaned and refused. “I beg you,” he said, “if any comrade will listen to me, do not tell me to eat or drink. I am weighed down with grief, and I will stay fasting until the sun goes down.”

findings.issue: Candidate opens the sailors' simile with 'Sailors at sea sometimes see', adding 'sometimes' and recasting Butler's 'As the light seen by sailors...even so'; both halves survive, so not a defect.
Candidate adds the rhetorical 'Think of it:' before 'many fewer Achaeans would have bitten the dust'; harmless filler not in the source.
